lesson_title: The Egg, the Duvet and the Crumple Zone: Momentum & Impulse
hook_text: Throw an egg at a wall — it smashes. Throw it at a duvet — it survives. Same egg, same speed.
clip_script: Throw an egg at a brick wall and it smashes. Throw the same egg, just as hard, at a duvet on the washing line, and it survives. Same egg, same speed, same change in momentum. So what saved it? Time. Against the wall, all that momentum is wiped out in a millisecond, and squeezing the change into a tiny time demands a huge force. The duvet gives way, and the same change takes half a second instead. Same change, a thousand times more time, a thousand times less force. Now look around: that trick is everywhere. An airbag is a duvet for your face. A crumple zone is a car agreeing to be squashed so the stop stretches out. The gravel bed at the bottom of a mountain pass is a duvet for a runaway truck. A fielder pulling the hands back on a hard catch, a netball player bending her knees on landing — all buying time to shrink the force. That's the impulse-momentum theorem, and it's the first equation of matric physics: force times time equals change in momentum. Fix the change, stretch the time, and the force has nowhere to go but down.
visual_style: Split screen of an egg meeting a brick wall and an egg sinking into a hanging duvet, force arrows shrinking as the stop stretches; quick cuts to an airbag, a crumple zone folding and gravel spraying in an arrestor bed.
mood: Playful, mischievous, then suddenly practical — physics that saves lives.
pacing: Sharp smash to open, slow-motion duvet catch, rapid-fire montage of safety devices, calm one-line close.
